# Finding the Antiderivative of -3*exp(x)*cos(x)

## Setting Up Integration by Parts

I need to compute ∫ -3*exp(x)*cos(x) dx = -3 * ∫ exp(x)*cos(x) dx

Let I = ∫ exp(x)*cos(x) dx

**First integration by parts:**
- u = cos(x), dv = exp(x) dx
- du = -sin(x) dx, v = exp(x)

$$I = \text{exp}(x)\cdot\cos(x) + \int \text{exp}(x)\cdot\sin(x)\, dx$$

**Second integration by parts** (on ∫ exp(x)·sin(x) dx):
- u = sin(x), dv = exp(x) dx
- du = cos(x) dx, v = exp(x)

$$\int \text{exp}(x)\cdot\sin(x)\, dx = \text{exp}(x)\cdot\sin(x) - \int \text{exp}(x)\cdot\cos(x)\, dx = \text{exp}(x)\cdot\sin(x) - I$$

## Solving for I

Substituting back:

$$I = \text{exp}(x)\cdot\cos(x) + \text{exp}(x)\cdot\sin(x) - I$$

$$2I = \text{exp}(x)\cdot\cos(x) + \text{exp}(x)\cdot\sin(x)$$

$$I = \frac{\text{exp}(x)\cdot(\cos(x) + \sin(x))}{2}$$

## Final Answer

Multiplying by -3:

$$\int -3\cdot\text{exp}(x)\cdot\cos(x)\, dx = -\frac{3}{2}\cdot\text{exp}(x)\cdot\cos(x) - \frac{3}{2}\cdot\text{exp}(x)\cdot\sin(x) + C$$

**Verification by differentiation:**
$$\frac{d}{dx}\left[-\frac{3}{2}\text{exp}(x)\cos(x) - \frac{3}{2}\text{exp}(x)\sin(x)\right] = -3\text{exp}(x)\cos(x) \checkmark$$

<answer>-3*exp(x)*cos(x)/2 - 3*exp(x)*sin(x)/2 + C</answer>

Then du = -sin(x) dx, v = exp(x)

Now for ∫exp(x)*sin(x) dx:

Then du = cos(x) dx, v = exp(x)

∫exp(x)*sin(x) dx = exp(x)*sin(x) - ∫exp(x)*cos(x) dx
= exp(x)*sin(x) - I

So:

2I = exp(x)*cos(x) + exp(x)*sin(x)

So ∫-3*exp(x)*cos(x) dx = -3 * exp(x)*(cos(x) + sin(x))/2 + C

= -3*exp(x)*cos(x)/2 - 3*exp(x)*sin(x)/2 + C

Let me verify by differentiating:
d/dx[-3*exp(x)*cos(x)/2 - 3*exp(x)*sin(x)/2]
= -3/2 * [exp(x)*cos(x) + exp(x)*(-sin(x))] - 3/2 * [exp(x)*sin(x) + exp(x)*cos(x)]
= -3/2 * [exp(x)*cos(x) - exp(x)*sin(x)] - 3/2 * [exp(x)*sin(x) + exp(x)*cos(x)]
= -3/2 * exp(x)*cos(x) + 3/2 * exp(x)*sin(x) - 3/2 * exp(x)*sin(x) - 3/2 * exp(x)*cos(x)

So the answer is -3*exp(x)*cos(x)/2 - 3*exp(x)*sin(x)/2 + C
